ModelVariations.Description: Gulfstar reused and evolved hull concepts across trawlers, motorsailers and motor yachts; Mk II and later motor-yacht generations can differ materially in layout, structure and speed.

ModelCharacter: An unusual American trawler built on the same soft-chined, ballasted semi-displacement hull as Gulfstar's 36 Motorsailer. Twin small Perkins diesels, a deep keel and moderate beam make it a slow, economical powerboat with distinctly sailboat-like hull behavior rather than a conventional boxy Taiwan trawler.
DesignLineage: The Gulfstar 36 Trawler was produced from 1972–1976 on the same hull used for the Gulfstar 36 Motorsailer.
The powerboat identity is legitimate: the Trawler received twin diesels, powerboat deck/helm arrangements and no dependence on a sailing rig.
In 1975 Gulfstar introduced the 36 Mk II with a raised aft deck, full-beam master, enlarged flybridge, larger rudders and redesigned teak interior.
The 36 Trawler and 36 Motorsailer therefore share hull lineage but remain materially different factory configurations and B-Atlas scopes.
OwnershipCharacter: Exceptionally economical at 7–8 knots and mechanically simple despite twin engines because the original Perkins installations are low-output. Age, ballast/keel structure, old tanks, windows, decks and insurance on a 50-year-old boat matter more than performance machinery.

The Yarmouth is one of three current cruising layouts—Yarmouth, Halifax and Digby—sharing the 246 hull but differing mainly in galley, dinette and head placement.
